metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source with a deployable WSGI entry point is present (helpdesk/settings.py defines ROOT_URLCONF and INSTALLED_APPS; tickets/views.py defines HTTP view functions), with no multi-service layout, no library packaging manifest, and no resource-provisioning IaC. Classified as application.
metadata.archetype_justification: The service owns persistent state in PostgreSQL (DATABASES in helpdesk/settings.py, direct queries against tickets_ticket in tickets/views.py) and exposes entity CRUD through django.contrib.admin alongside its read views. No queue consumers and no multi-service coordination were found. Classified as stateful-crud.

surface_flags.rationale: A PostgreSQL store is configured and queried in-repo (persistent data store, at-rest surface). HTTP view functions constitute an API surface. No Dockerfile, Kubernetes/Helm manifests, or Terraform/CDK/CloudFormation exist anywhere in the repository, so no deployed workload and no AWS resource provisioning are owned here; README.md documents a manual git-pull deployment onto a single EC2 instance, which also makes the deployment single-instance.

classification_consistency_check.reason: Overall score 1.24 yields the Not Ready band while 10 High findings match the 2-11 High → Remediation Required tier. The repository is uniformly immature (29 of 31 findings are score 1), which drags the numeric mean below 1.5, but 21 of those score-1 questions are non-core and map to Medium severity, capping the High count at 10. Surface gating and archetype calibration were re-applied and do not remove the divergence: the gaps are broad rather than concentrated in core questions. Documented rather than corrected.

categories.scoring_note: (1+1+1+1+1+1) / 6 = 1.00 — SEC-Q1 excluded (Not Evaluated, no account-level IaC).
(1+1+1+1+1+1) / 6 = 1.00 — OPS-Q5, OPS-Q7, OPS-Q9 excluded (Not Evaluated, surface flags).

top_gaps.title: Secrets Management
top_gaps.gap: Django SECRET_KEY and the database password are committed in plaintext in helpdesk/settings.py.
top_gaps.impact: Credentials are exposed to anyone with repo access and persist in git history; session/CSRF signing keys are forgeable. Blocks safe redeployment until rotated.

top_gaps.title: Database Engine Version and EOL
top_gaps.gap: PostgreSQL 9.1 (past EOL) with no version pinning in any IaC — the version exists only as prose in README.md.
top_gaps.impact: No security patches for the data tier; a managed-database migration must include a major-version engine jump.

top_gaps.title: Managed Databases
top_gaps.gap: PostgreSQL is self-managed on the same EC2 instance as the application.
top_gaps.impact: No automated failover, patching, or managed backups; app and data share a single failure domain.

top_gaps.title: CI/CD Automation
top_gaps.gap: Deployment is a manual git pull plus Apache restart; no pipeline definitions exist in the repo.
top_gaps.impact: No build, test, or rollback gate, which makes every other modernization step unsafe to execute.

top_gaps.title: Infrastructure as Code Coverage
top_gaps.gap: No Terraform, CDK, CloudFormation, Helm, or Kubernetes definitions; all infrastructure is manually created.
top_gaps.impact: Infrastructure is non-reproducible, blocking environment parity, disaster recovery, and automated deployment.

findings.title: Managed Compute
findings.description: All compute runs on a single raw EC2 instance: README.md documents Apache 2.2 + mod_wsgi on Ubuntu 12.04 with PostgreSQL co-resident. No Dockerfile, no ECS/EKS/Lambda definitions, and no container image references exist in the repository, so managed-compute adoption is zero and capacity, patching, and availability are all manual.
findings.gap: Zero managed-compute adoption; the application shares a single unmanaged host with its database.
findings.recommendation: After the Python 3 / Django runtime upgrade, containerize the WSGI app onto ECS/Fargate behind an ALB and move PostgreSQL to RDS. Do not containerize the Python 2.7 runtime as-is.

findings.title: Managed Databases
findings.description: The only database is a self-managed PostgreSQL 9.1 instance on 127.0.0.1 — the same EC2 host as the application (DATABASES in helpdesk/settings.py, corroborated by README.md). No aws_rds_*, aws_dynamodb_*, or other managed-database resource is defined. Surface gate has_persistent_data_store is true, so the question was evaluated.
findings.gap: No managed database: no automatic failover, no managed backups or patching, and no isolation between the app and data failure domains.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL (or Aurora PostgreSQL) at a current supported major version with Multi-AZ, automated backups, and PITR; use AWS DMS for the move and source credentials from Secrets Manager.

findings.title: Workflow Orchestration
findings.description: Scored against the stateful-crud archetype column. No workflow orchestration exists — no aws_sfn_*, no Temporal or Camunda client, no workflow definitions. Any ticket-lifecycle sequencing lives as inline application logic; tickets/views.py contains request-scoped query logic only. For a stateless-utility this question would have been Not Evaluated by design, but a service owning ticket status lifecycle is expected to have managed orchestration for multi-step operations.
findings.gap: No orchestration primitive, so ticket lifecycle steps have no managed retry, error handling, or execution visibility.
findings.recommendation: Low priority relative to the platform gaps. If ticket escalation or SLA-breach handling is formalized, implement it in Step Functions or EventBridge Scheduler rather than inline view code.

findings.title: Async Messaging and Streaming
findings.description: Scored against the stateful-crud archetype column, where managed messaging for cross-service state changes is the Score-4 bar. No managed or self-managed messaging exists (no SQS/SNS/EventBridge/Kinesis/MSK resources, no messaging SDK imports). The only outbound integration is a blocking SMTP relay (EMAIL_HOST 'exchange.acme-corp.internal', port 25) invoked synchronously in the request path. Under a stateless-utility or data-gateway archetype synchronous-only would have been correct by design and scored 4.
findings.gap: Ticket notifications leave the system over a synchronous SMTP call on the request thread, with no queue, buffer, or retry, so Exchange latency degrades the web tier directly.
findings.recommendation: Move notification delivery behind SQS with a worker consumer and send through Amazon SES instead of a direct SMTP relay, so delivery failures retry out-of-band.

findings.title: Network Security
findings.description: No network surface is defined anywhere in the repository — no aws_vpc, aws_subnet, or aws_security_group, and no Kubernetes NetworkPolicy or service-mesh rules. README.md describes a single EC2 instance serving Apache directly with the database on the same host, with no VPC, subnet tiering, or segmentation. DEBUG = True additionally exposes stack traces to any caller that reaches the listener.
findings.gap: No private subnets, least-privilege security groups, or tier segmentation; app and data tiers share one host with no network boundary or blast-radius containment.
findings.recommendation: Define a custom VPC in IaC with public (ALB only) and private (app, data) subnet tiers, place the app in private subnets behind the ALB, restrict the database security group to the app security group only, and set DEBUG = False.

findings.title: API Entry Point
findings.description: The service is exposed directly by Apache + mod_wsgi on the instance (README.md). No API Gateway, AppSync, ALB, or CloudFront resource is defined — no aws_api_gateway_*, aws_apigatewayv2_*, or aws_lb_* exists anywhere in the repository.
findings.gap: No managed entry point, so no throttling, centralized authentication, request validation, health-check-based traffic removal, or TLS termination under configuration control.
findings.recommendation: Place an Application Load Balancer in front of the app with HTTPS listeners and health checks during containerization; add API Gateway only if throttling or request validation for programmatic consumers is required.

findings.title: Auto-Scaling
findings.description: No auto-scaling of any kind: no aws_autoscaling_* or aws_appautoscaling_* resources, no scaling policies, and no min/max capacity settings. README.md describes one statically provisioned EC2 instance hosting both the app and the database.
findings.gap: Capacity is fixed; traffic spikes degrade the single instance and its co-resident database, and idle periods cannot scale down.
findings.recommendation: Once on ECS/Fargate, configure service auto-scaling with target tracking on request count per target and CPU, and scale the data tier independently via RDS sizing or Aurora replicas.

findings.title: Backup and Recovery
findings.description: Surface gate has_persistent_data_store is true, so the question was evaluated. README.md documents 'no backups beyond a daily pg_dump cron' — a logical dump of the main production database only. No backup_retention_period, point_in_time_recovery, aws_backup_plan, S3 versioning, or EBS snapshot lifecycle policy is defined, and no restore testing is documented.
findings.gap: Backups cover only the main database with no PITR, no defined retention, no cross-region copy, and no tested restore; recovery point is up to 24 hours and the dump shares the host it protects.
findings.recommendation: Fold backup into the RDS migration: enable automated backups with explicit retention and PITR, add an AWS Backup plan with cross-region copy, and schedule a documented restore rehearsal into a scratch instance.

findings.title: Infrastructure as Code Coverage
findings.description: No IaC exists. Searched the repository root and both package directories for *.tf/*.tfvars, CDK entry points and cdk.json, CloudFormation/SAM templates, Chart.yaml/values.yaml, and kustomization.yaml — none found. The repository contains only README.md, .gitignore, helpdesk/settings.py, and tickets/views.py, so compute, networking, the PostgreSQL store, DNS, secrets, and monitoring are all manually created.
findings.gap: 0% IaC coverage (pure ClickOps): infrastructure is not reproducible, reviewable, or recoverable.
findings.recommendation: Codify the target state (VPC and subnet tiers, ALB, ECS service, RDS instance, Secrets Manager secrets, CloudWatch alarms, backup plan) in Terraform or CDK, written for the target architecture rather than reverse-engineered from the current instance.

evidence.file: *.tf, cdk.json, Chart.yaml, kustomization.yaml (searched repository root, helpdesk/, tickets/)

findings.title: CI/CD Automation
findings.description: No pipeline definitions exist. Searched for .github/workflows/, .gitlab-ci.yml, Jenkinsfile, buildspec.yml, appspec.yml, and CodePipeline definitions in IaC — none found. README.md states deployment is 'git pull on the server + manual apache restart'.
findings.gap: Deployments are fully manual with no build, no automated test gate, no immutable artifact, no deployment record, and no rollback path, on either the application or the infrastructure track.
findings.recommendation: Build a pipeline in stages: install and lint on push, run unit and integration tests, build a container image to ECR, deploy to ECS with health checks and automated rollback, and add IaC plan/apply as a parallel track with dependency and SAST scanning gates.

findings.title: Programming Languages
findings.description: Python 2.7 with Django 1.4. tickets/views.py uses Python 2 syntax that will not parse under Python 3 (print statement), and helpdesk/settings.py uses the Django 1.4-era MIDDLEWARE_CLASSES setting and django.db.backends.postgresql_psycopg2 engine path. README.md confirms Python 2.7 (EOL Jan 2020) and Django 1.4 (EOL 2015). No AWS SDK is present and no dependency manifest exists to pin either.
findings.gap: Compound regression on both calibration axes — the language runtime and the web framework are both end-of-life and unsupported, with no reproducible dependency set (no requirements.txt, system-wide packages, no virtualenv).
findings.recommendation: Treat the runtime upgrade as the first work item: capture the current dependency set into a pinned requirements.txt in a virtualenv, then upgrade to Python 3.11+ and a supported Django release, porting print statements, render_to_response, MIDDLEWARE_CLASSES, and the raw SQL call sites.

findings.title: Monolith vs Microservices
findings.description: A single Django deployable with identifiable module boundaries — a project package (helpdesk/) and one application package (tickets/) registered in INSTALLED_APPS. The modules do not own their data: tickets/views.py issues raw connection.cursor() SQL directly against the tickets_ticket table in the single shared schema, with no ORM model layer or data-access interface mediating it.
findings.gap: Module structure exists but data access bypasses it, so no boundary is enforceable — this is the Score-2 pattern (identifiable modules, shared schema, direct SQL) rather than Score 3 (modules own data behind interfaces).
findings.recommendation: Introduce Django ORM models owned by the tickets app and route all access through them, removing raw cursor usage; this establishes the module data contract and eliminates the SQL injection vectors. Full decomposition is not recommended at this size.

findings.title: Async vs Sync Communication
findings.description: Scored against the stateful-crud archetype column, whose Score-4 bar is 50%+ async for cross-service state propagation. All communication is synchronous: tickets/views.py performs blocking database queries inline, and the only outbound integration is a synchronous SMTP relay to on-prem Exchange. No message publishing, queue consumers, event handlers, or event source mappings exist. Under a stateless-utility archetype this would have been Not Evaluated by design, and under data-gateway sync-dominant reads would have scored 4.
findings.gap: 100% synchronous: outward state propagation (ticket notifications) runs over a blocking call to an external system, so external latency or failure surfaces directly as request latency or errors.
findings.recommendation: Introduce managed async for the notification path specifically — publish ticket state changes to SQS/EventBridge and deliver email from a worker via SES. Keep read paths synchronous; the goal is decoupling the outbound dependency.

findings.title: Long-Running Process Handling
findings.description: Scored against the stateful-crud archetype column, whose Score-4 bar is that all operations over 30 seconds run as async jobs with status polling or callbacks. Every operation is synchronous regardless of duration: ticket_search runs an unbounded LIKE '%...%' scan with no LIMIT or pagination, and ticket_list selects all matching tickets ordered by created with no bound. No background job framework, job status API, polling, or callback pattern exists. Under a stateless-utility archetype this would have been Not Evaluated by design.
findings.gap: No async job infrastructure and at least one query path whose latency grows with table size on the request thread, so searches will eventually exceed the web server timeout with no way to offload them.
findings.recommendation: Add pagination and LIMIT bounds to both query paths immediately and index the searched columns; implement any later heavy operation (bulk export, reporting) as a queued job with a status endpoint.

findings.title: API Versioning Strategy
findings.description: No versioning of any kind. helpdesk/settings.py points ROOT_URLCONF at helpdesk.urls, and the view functions in tickets/views.py carry no version prefix, version header handling, or versioning annotation. No OpenAPI/Swagger specification and no changelog exist in the repository.
findings.gap: Any response-shape change breaks all consumers simultaneously with no migration window; ticket_search returns hand-built HTML rather than a versioned, content-negotiated payload.
findings.recommendation: If any programmatic consumer exists or is planned, introduce /v1/ URL prefixes, publish an OpenAPI specification, and return JSON from data endpoints instead of string-concatenated HTML.

findings.title: Service Discovery
findings.description: All endpoints are hard-coded in source. helpdesk/settings.py embeds the database host ('127.0.0.1', port 5432) and the mail relay ('exchange.acme-corp.internal', port 25) as literals in version-controlled code. No AWS Cloud Map, Istio, or Consul is present, and not even environment-variable indirection — os is imported but never used for configuration.
findings.gap: Endpoints cannot change without a code change and redeploy, so relocating the database to an RDS endpoint requires editing source, which blocks environment parity.
findings.recommendation: Externalize all endpoints to environment variables or SSM Parameter Store and source database credentials from Secrets Manager. Adopt AWS Cloud Map only if the service count grows; for a single service, configuration externalization is the right scope.

findings.title: Unstructured Data Storage
findings.description: Unstructured content is served from local instance disk: README.md states 'Static Files: Served from local disk, no CDN'. No aws_s3_bucket resource, no S3 SDK usage, no Textract or document-parsing library, and no STATICFILES_STORAGE/DEFAULT_FILE_STORAGE override in helpdesk/settings.py, so Django's default filesystem storage applies to any attachment uploads as well.
findings.gap: Static assets and any attachment content live on the single instance's filesystem — not durable beyond the instance, not shareable across instances (blocking horizontal scaling), not independently backed up, and not accessible to extraction pipelines.
findings.recommendation: Move static assets to S3 fronted by CloudFront and configure Django's storage backend accordingly; store attachment uploads in S3 with server-side encryption. Add Textract-based extraction only if attachment search becomes a requirement.

findings.title: Unified Data Access Layer
findings.description: There is no data access layer. tickets/views.py imports django.db.connection at module level and both view functions open their own cursor and execute hand-written SQL against tickets_ticket. No repository or DAO module exists and no Django ORM models are defined. The SQL is assembled by %-formatting request parameters into the query string in both functions, so the same pattern also produces SQL injection (status and q come from request.GET unescaped).
findings.gap: Query logic is scattered into the presentation layer with no single point of data contract, so schema changes touch every view and there is no place to enforce parameterization or access control.
findings.recommendation: Define Django ORM models for the ticket schema and route all access through them; where raw SQL is genuinely required, confine it to a single repository module using parameterized queries (cursor.execute(sql, params)). This is the highest-value single refactor — it establishes the data contract and closes the injection vulnerability together.

findings.title: Database Engine Version and EOL
findings.description: The engine version is not pinned in any configuration or IaC. helpdesk/settings.py specifies only the driver (django.db.backends.postgresql_psycopg2) with no version constraint, and there is no Terraform engine_version, docker-compose image tag, or Helm values file. The version is recorded only as prose in README.md: 'PostgreSQL 9.1 (EOL)'.
findings.gap: The production engine is past end of life and unpatched, and because the version lives nowhere in code there is no way to detect drift or govern upgrades; no upgrade procedure, downtime window, or rollback plan is documented.
findings.recommendation: Pin the engine version explicitly in IaC as part of the RDS migration and target a currently supported PostgreSQL major version. Validate the 9.1 to current major-version jump against a restored dump in staging first, and document the upgrade/rollback procedure alongside the IaC.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest
findings.description: Surface gate has_at_rest_data_surface is true, so the question was evaluated. No encryption at rest is configured anywhere: no aws_kms_key resource, no kms_key_id on any data store, and no encryption settings in helpdesk/settings.py. The database is self-managed PostgreSQL on local EC2 storage and README.md documents static files on local disk; the daily pg_dump output is likewise unencrypted.
findings.gap: Helpdesk ticket data (internal user identifiers and free-text issue descriptions) and its backups sit unencrypted on instance storage, with no key management, rotation policy, or key-access audit trail.
findings.recommendation: Enable encryption at rest with a customer-managed KMS key when migrating to RDS, enable SSE-KMS on the S3 buckets created for static assets and backups, encrypt EBS volumes for any remaining instance storage, and document a key rotation policy.

findings.title: API Authentication
findings.description: Neither view function enforces authentication. tickets/views.py defines ticket_list and ticket_search with no @login_required decorator, no permission check, and no token validation — both read ticket data for any caller that reaches them. helpdesk/settings.py installs SessionMiddleware and AuthenticationMiddleware, which populate request.user, but populating identity is not enforcing it and no authorization is performed. There is no OAuth2/JWT handling and no API Gateway authorizer.
findings.gap: 100% of the endpoints in this repository are unauthenticated and return business data, and with no network segmentation in evidence (INF-Q5) there is no compensating isolation control either.
findings.recommendation: Apply @login_required or an equivalent permission-checking decorator to every view returning ticket data, add a project-wide default-deny check so new views are protected by omission, and front the service with an ALB/API Gateway federated to a central IdP.

findings.title: Centralized Identity Integration
findings.description: The application manages its own authentication entirely. helpdesk/settings.py installs django.contrib.auth with the default local user model and session middleware, and there is no aws_cognito_* resource, no OIDC or SAML configuration, no federation backend, and no SSO settings anywhere in the repository.
findings.gap: Credentials and user lifecycle are owned locally and independently of the corporate directory, so there is no SSO, no central MFA enforcement, and no centralized deprovisioning; password hashing is whatever Django 1.4 defaulted to.
findings.recommendation: Federate authentication to the corporate IdP via OIDC/SAML — Amazon Cognito as the broker in front of the existing directory is the low-friction option — and retire local password storage. Sequence after the Django upgrade, since modern federation libraries require a supported release.

findings.title: Secrets Management
findings.description: Plaintext credentials are committed to source control. helpdesk/settings.py contains the database password as a literal (annotated in the file as 'plaintext db password') and the Django SECRET_KEY as a literal (annotated 'Secret key committed to source control'); README.md independently flags the SECRET_KEY exposure. No aws_secretsmanager_* resource, Vault client, or environment-variable indirection exists — os is imported but never used.
findings.gap: Both secrets are readable by anyone with repository access and persist in git history even if edited now. The SECRET_KEY signs sessions and CSRF tokens, so its exposure permits session forgery; the database password grants direct data access. Neither is rotated.
findings.recommendation: Treat both as compromised: rotate the database password and the SECRET_KEY (accepting session invalidation), store them in AWS Secrets Manager, and load them at startup from the environment or the Secrets Manager API. Enable rotation for the database credential (RDS-managed once migrated) and add a pre-commit secret scanner. Purging git history does not remove the need to rotate.

findings.title: Compute Hardening and Patching
findings.description: No patching strategy or vulnerability scanning is in evidence: no aws_ssm_patch_baseline, no SSM Agent configuration, no Inspector or Snyk integration, no hardened base image reference (CIS, Bottlerocket), and no EC2 Image Builder pipeline. No dependency-update automation exists either — .github/dependabot.yml, .github/dependabot.yaml, renovate.json, .renovaterc, .renovaterc.json, and .github/renovate.json were all searched and are absent. README.md documents Ubuntu 12.04 and Apache 2.2 (both EOL) with system-wide packages and no virtualenv.
findings.gap: The entire stack below the application — OS, web server, runtime, framework — is end-of-life and unpatchable, with no automation that would surface or remediate a reported vulnerability, and no pinned dependency set to even enumerate.
findings.recommendation: Replace rather than patch the current host: build on a current Amazon Linux or managed container base image, enable ECR image scanning (or Inspector for instances), enable SSM Patch Manager for remaining EC2, and add Dependabot or Renovate once requirements.txt exists.

findings.title: Application Security Pipeline
findings.description: No security scanning exists, because no pipeline exists. Searched for CI definitions (.github/workflows/, buildspec.yml, Jenkinsfile, .gitlab-ci.yml), SAST configuration (SonarQube, Semgrep, CodeGuru, .snyk), dependency scanning (Dependabot/Renovate config, pip-audit, safety), and container scanning — none found.
findings.gap: No automated validation step of any kind, so defects reach production undetected. The SQL injection in tickets/views.py is exactly the class of defect a basic SAST rule flags on first run, and it has persisted.
findings.recommendation: Once the CI pipeline exists, add dependency scanning (pip-audit plus Dependabot/Renovate), Python SAST (Bandit or Semgrep) configured to fail the build on high-confidence injection findings, and ECR image scanning after containerization. Make the SAST gate blocking.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing
findings.description: No tracing instrumentation of any kind: no OpenTelemetry or X-Ray SDK usage, no traceparent/X-Amzn-Trace-Id propagation, and no tracing middleware in helpdesk/settings.py (MIDDLEWARE_CLASSES contains only Django's common, session, and auth middleware). The only diagnostic output in the codebase is a leftover debugging print statement in tickets/views.py writing a user-supplied search term to stdout.
findings.gap: No request-level visibility, so latency cannot be attributed between the web tier, the database query, and the SMTP relay — exactly the attribution needed before and after the planned migration. DEBUG = True delivers diagnostics as stack traces to end users instead of to an observability backend.
findings.recommendation: Instrument with OpenTelemetry (Django auto-instrumentation plus the psycopg2 instrumentor) exporting to X-Ray or an OTLP collector, propagate trace headers from the ALB inward, remove the debug print, and set DEBUG = False with structured logging to CloudWatch Logs.

findings.title: SLO Definitions
findings.description: Surface gate passes (has_api_surface=true, has_persistent_data_store=true), so the question was evaluated. No monitoring artifacts exist at all: no SLO definition files, no CloudWatch alarms in IaC (there is no IaC), no latency or error-rate thresholds, no error budget tracking, and no dashboard definitions. Score 2 would require at least threshold-based alarms implying implicit SLOs; nothing of the kind is present.
findings.gap: No definition of acceptable service levels for the ticket list or search journeys and no measurement, so degradation is invisible until users report it.
findings.recommendation: Define availability and p95 latency targets for the two user journeys, implement them as CloudWatch alarms declared in IaC once the ALB and RDS instance exist, and track an error budget. Sequence after instrumentation (OPS-Q1) and IaC (INF-Q10). Note that SLO tooling often lives outside the repo, so this score reflects only in-repo evidence.

evidence.file: SLO definitions, CloudWatch alarm declarations, dashboards (searched repository root, helpdesk/, tickets/)

findings.title: Business Metrics
findings.description: No custom metrics are published: no put_metric_data calls, no StatsD/Prometheus client, no metrics middleware, and no dashboard definitions. tickets/views.py emits no telemetry beyond a single print statement.
findings.gap: Nothing is measured about helpdesk outcomes — ticket volume by priority, time-to-resolution, reopen rate, search success rate — so there is no data with which to prioritize modernization work or demonstrate its effect.
findings.recommendation: Emit a small set of business metrics (tickets created/resolved by priority, time-to-first-response, search result-count distribution) to CloudWatch via EMF or the SDK and chart them beside infrastructure metrics. Add during the application refactor so emission points land in the new data access layer.

findings.title: Anomaly Detection and Alerting
findings.description: No alerting is configured: no CloudWatch alarms or anomaly detectors (no IaC exists to declare them), no SNS alert topics, and no PagerDuty/OpsGenie integration. The only notification configuration is the Django ADMINS tuple in helpdesk/settings.py, which with DEBUG = True does not even send error mail — Django suppresses admin error emails while DEBUG is on.
findings.gap: No alerting at all, anomaly-based or static, so an outage of the single instance or its co-resident database is detected only by user reports.
findings.recommendation: Start with static threshold alarms on ALB 5xx rate, p95 target response time, and RDS CPU/storage/connections routed to SNS and an on-call tool, then layer CloudWatch anomaly detection on error rate and latency once a baseline exists. Setting DEBUG = False restores Django admin error mail as an interim backstop.

findings.title: Integration Testing
findings.description: No automated tests exist in the repository. The complete inventory is README.md, .gitignore, helpdesk/settings.py, and tickets/views.py — no tests/ directory, no test_*.py or *_test.py file, no tickets/tests.py, no contract or API test suite, and no CI pipeline to run tests in. README.md acknowledges 'No tests beyond a couple of stale unit tests'; those are not present here.
findings.gap: Zero automated verification of the ticket list and search workflows and no pipeline to run tests in — the largest risk multiplier for the recommended work, since the Python 2 to 3 upgrade, the Django major-version upgrade, the raw-SQL-to-ORM refactor, and the PostgreSQL migration would all run with no regression safety net.
findings.recommendation: Write integration tests for the two user journeys (ticket list filtered by status, ticket search) against an ephemeral PostgreSQL container using Django's test client, and wire them into the CI pipeline as a blocking gate before starting the runtime upgrade.

evidence.file: tests/, test_*.py, tickets/tests.py (searched repository root, helpdesk/, tickets/)

findings.title: Observability Ownership
findings.description: No observability assets exist to own and no ownership metadata is defined: no CODEOWNERS file, no dashboard or alarm definitions, no SLO files with named owners, and no team tags (no AWS resources are declared in-repo to tag). The only ownership signal is the Django ADMINS entry ('IT Ops', 'it-ops@acme-corp.internal') in helpdesk/settings.py — a shared mailbox with no per-asset attribution.
findings.gap: Monitoring is reactive and fragmented, with no service dashboard, no alarms, and no named owner for any observability asset, so there is no attribution path from a symptom to a responsible owner during an incident.
findings.recommendation: Add a CODEOWNERS file covering the application and the IaC that will define its alarms and dashboards, create a per-service dashboard declared in IaC, and attach owner tags to the AWS resources created during migration. Sequence after OPS-Q1/OPS-Q2 so there are assets to own.

evaluations.title: High Availability and Fault Isolation
evaluations.reason: has_deployed_workload=false — no Dockerfile with deployment manifests and no IaC defining compute, so there is no deployed workload requiring HA evaluation in this repo. README.md describes a single-instance, single-AZ deployment; HA should be designed in under INF-Q1 and INF-Q2.

evaluations.title: Stored Procedures and Schema Complexity
evaluations.reason: Score 4 — no stored procedures, triggers, or proprietary SQL. No *.sql files and no CREATE PROCEDURE/TRIGGER/FUNCTION anywhere; the raw SQL in tickets/views.py is portable ANSI-style PostgreSQL with no dialect features, and all business logic sits in the application layer.

evaluations.title: Audit Logging
evaluations.reason: has_iac_provisioning_aws_resources=false and no account-level IaC scope. CloudTrail is an AWS account-level service provisioned once per account or organization; evaluation belongs in the foundation/account-level infrastructure repo.

pathways.name: Move to Cloud Native
pathways.key_trigger_criteria: APP-Q2 < 3 (primary) AND at least one of INF-Q1 < 3, APP-Q3 < 3, APP-Q4 < 3

triggering_questions.note: Primary — single Django deployable with modules that do not own their data
Supporting — all compute on a single raw EC2 instance
Supporting — 100% synchronous communication including blocking SMTP
Supporting — unbounded synchronous queries, no async job surface

detail.current_state: Single Django 1.4 deployable on one EC2 instance with a co-resident PostgreSQL; identifiable app packages but raw SQL from views against the shared schema; all paths synchronous including a blocking SMTP relay.
immediate_actions: Pin dependencies into requirements.txt inside a virtualenv
Upgrade Python 2.7 to 3.x and Django 1.4 to a supported release (prerequisite for any supported container base image)
Replace raw cursor SQL with ORM models to establish module data ownership
Decouple the outbound notification path onto SQS + SES

pathways.name: Move to Containers
pathways.key_trigger_criteria: INF-Q1 < 3 AND no container definitions found in discovery

triggering_questions.note: Primary — EC2/VM-based compute only; no Dockerfile, docker-compose, or Kubernetes manifests found, and the guard does not apply because no Lambda/Fargate/ECS compute exists

detail.current_state: One EC2 instance on Ubuntu 12.04 running Apache 2.2 + mod_wsgi, not described by any IaC. Against containerization: Python 2.7/Django 1.4 have no supported base image, dependencies are system-wide with no requirements.txt, static files are on local disk, and configuration and secrets are hardcoded in settings.py. In favor: a standard WSGI app with a single listener.
detail.migration_approach: Refactor-then-containerize. Lift-and-containerize would freeze an unsupported runtime into the image. Sequence: pin dependencies, upgrade runtime and framework, externalize config and secrets, author the Dockerfile and ECS task definition, move static assets to S3 + CloudFront.
immediate_actions: Create a pinned requirements.txt and virtualenv
Complete the Python 3 / Django upgrade before authoring any Dockerfile
Externalize DB host, SMTP host, SECRET_KEY, and DB password out of settings.py
Author the Dockerfile and ECS/Fargate task definition in IaC

pathways.name: Move to Open Source
pathways.key_trigger_criteria: DATA-Q4 < 3 AND commercial DB engines detected in the INF-Q2 finding

triggering_questions.note: DATA-Q4 = 4 meets threshold — no stored procedures, triggers, or proprietary SQL; all logic is in the application layer

pathways.not_triggered_reason: The primary condition is not met (DATA-Q4 = 4) and no commercial database engine was detected — the data tier is already open-source PostgreSQL, so there is no licensed engine or proprietary SQL to migrate off.

triggering_questions.note: Primary — self-managed PostgreSQL on the same EC2 host as the application
Supporting — PostgreSQL 9.1 past EOL with no version pinning in any IaC

detail.current_state: Self-managed PostgreSQL 9.1 on 127.0.0.1, co-resident with the application. Manual patching, failover, and backups; the only backup is a daily pg_dump cron with no restore testing. Data access is raw, string-formatted SQL from view functions with no ORM layer, so two query paths are also injection-vulnerable.
immediate_actions: Validate the 9.1 to current major-version jump against a restored pg_dump in a staging RDS instance
Convert raw SQL call sites to parameterized queries or the Django ORM
Provision RDS PostgreSQL Multi-AZ with automated backups, PITR, and a customer-managed KMS key in IaC
Repoint DATABASES HOST at the RDS endpoint and source credentials from Secrets Manager

pathways.name: Move to Managed Analytics
pathways.key_trigger_criteria: INF-Q4 < 3 AND evidence of data processing workloads must exist (contextual guard)

triggering_questions.note: Below threshold, but blocked by the contextual guard

pathways.not_triggered_reason: Contextual guard blocks the pathway: no streaming, ETL, data pipeline, or analytics artifacts were found in discovery — no Kinesis/MSK/Kafka configuration, no Glue jobs, no Airflow DAGs, no data lake or Athena usage. This is an internal CRUD ticketing application with no data processing responsibilities, so managed analytics infrastructure would not address a real gap.

pathways.name: Move to Modern DevOps
pathways.key_trigger_criteria: INF-Q10 < 3 OR INF-Q11 < 3 (primary); OPS-Q5 < 3 and OPS-Q6 < 3 strengthen

triggering_questions.note: Primary — 0% IaC coverage; no Terraform, CDK, CloudFormation, Helm, or Kustomize artifacts
Primary — no pipeline definitions; deployment is a manual git pull plus Apache restart
Supporting — no automated tests exist and no CI pipeline to run them in

detail.current_state: Zero IaC and zero CI/CD. Every infrastructure category the service depends on is manually created. OPS-Q5 was Not Evaluated (no deployed workload in-repo), but README.md documents in-place direct-to-production changes with no traffic shifting, and no tests exist to gate them.
immediate_actions: Stand up a CI pipeline that installs, lints, and runs tests on every push
Add integration tests for ticket list and ticket search against an ephemeral PostgreSQL
Codify compute, networking, data store, and alarms in IaC
Add a deploy stage with health checks and automated rollback
Add dependency and SAST scanning as blocking gates

pathways.name: Move to AI
pathways.key_trigger_criteria: No AI/agent frameworks, vector DB, RAG, or agent eval framework — gated on AI/agent/LLM intent evidenced in the repository
pathways.not_triggered_reason: No AI/agent intent evidenced in the repository (no AI-related signal terms in dependencies, source, configuration, IaC, or documentation). README.md, helpdesk/settings.py, and tickets/views.py were scanned for the signal term list and contain no matches, so the primary trigger conditions were not evaluated.

decomposition_strategy.recommended_approach_rationale: The binding constraints are the EOL runtime, the plaintext secrets, the EOL self-managed database, and the absent pipeline — not module coupling. Fix the platform first and treat decomposition as optional and demand-driven.

approach_options.fit: Strong secondary fit — the app is ~76 lines across two Django apps serving an internal audience; replacing raw cursor SQL with app-owned ORM models captures most of the coupling benefit with no topology change.
Weak fit at current size — two view functions and one entity leave nothing meaningful to extract. Revisit if additional bounded contexts emerge.
Recommended — modernize the runtime and containerize, then extract only modules with a concrete independent-scaling or ownership driver (possibly none).
Recommended against — the application is functional and small; a rewrite carries feature-parity risk for no architectural return.

patterns.when: At the data boundary during the runtime upgrade — introduce ORM models for tickets_ticket so no new code issues raw SQL against the legacy schema.
When the view layer is rewritten — isolate ticket logic from the DB and SMTP adapters so email can move to SES/SQS without touching domain code.
Not applicable today — all state is in one database with no cross-service transactions. Revisit only if extraction occurs.
Optional; well-matched to ticket status history if audit requirements emerge. Not a prerequisite for any recommended step.

effort_factors.observed: Django app directories exist; boundaries identifiable (APP-Q2 = 2)
Raw cross-layer SQL against a single shared schema, no ORM models (DATA-Q2 = 1)
None — all logic in the application layer (DATA-Q4 = 4)

effort_factors.effect: Raises effort if async is introduced

decomposition_strategy.calibrated_estimate: Low to Medium overall, front-loaded into the Python 2.7 to 3 and Django 1.4 to current upgrade and into building the missing test and pipeline safety net. The decomposition component itself is near-zero given the small codebase and the absence of stored-procedure or cross-service transaction debt.
